memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Whenever they enter the tent of meeting, they shall wash with water so that they will not die. Also, when they approach the altar to minister by presenting a food offering to the Lord, they shall wash their hands and feet so that they will not die. This is to be a lasting ordinance for Aaron and his descendants for the generations to come." - Exodus 30:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The instruction is repeated with sobering weight: wash, so that you will not die. This was not optional hygiene. Approaching God without cleansing was genuinely dangerous. Every entry into the tent, every approach to the altar, required washing first.

We can lose this seriousness. Because grace is free, we sometimes treat approach to God as casual, forgetting that the way was opened at enormous cost. The priests were reminded twice daily that a holy God is not approached carelessly.

Yet notice the mercy in it. God did not say "stay away." He provided a basin. The command to wash was accompanied by the means of washing, always available, standing right there in the courtyard. God never demands cleanness without providing the water. The psalmist asked who may ascend the hill of the Lord, and answered: the one who has clean hands and a pure heart (Ps 24:3-4). We could never produce that ourselves — so God provided it in Christ. Take His holiness seriously, and take His provision gratefully.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Has my approach to God become casual rather than reverent?
Am I using the means of cleansing God has provided, or ignoring them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are holy, and You provided the very cleansing You require. Keep me from casualness, and thank You that in Christ I have clean hands to serve You. Amen.
